subject: IDB-001
statement: Climate observations can frame seasonal context, but this package does not estimate vector suitability, abundance, or disease incidence.

subject: IDB-002
statement: Standing-water and wetland context can identify a habitat interface, but vector response is not quantified.
notes: Hydrology is not a vector count or disease surface.

subject: IDB-004
statement: Vector ecology and pathogen-in-vector context do not establish human contact, exposure, infection, or clinical disease.

subject: IDB-010
statement: Water-system condition or flooding identifies an exposure opportunity only; contamination, exposure, infection, illness, and outbreak require separate evidence.

subject: IDB-009
statement: Water and energy infrastructure are generalized dependencies; facility condition and treatment performance are not modeled.
notes: No facility-specific burden or service assignment.

subject: IDB-013
statement: Food/freight connectivity is an interface for distribution and investigation, not evidence of shipment, contamination, or outbreak.
notes: No commodity route or outbreak claim.

subject: IDB-019
statement: Population concentration identifies a possible contact structure, not contact events, exposure, infection, or incidence.

subject: IDB-020
statement: Aggregate mobility can indicate possible connectivity, but commuting and movement are not transmission observations.

subject: IDB-021
statement: Indoor/community setting is a qualitative interface for respiratory systems; no density-to-incidence relationship is estimated.

subject: IDB-026
statement: Wildlife, domestic-animal, and occupational interfaces are pathway contexts; animal contact does not establish human infection or disease.
notes: Animal endpoint and human endpoint remain separate.

subject: IDB-031
statement: Surveillance intensity, testing, reporting, and laboratory participation change detection opportunity and do not equal incidence or burden.

subject: IDB-034
statement: Healthcare facility presence creates a care and detection interface; it does not establish facility-level disease burden.

subject: IDB-033
statement: Energy and communications dependencies may affect continuity of healthcare or surveillance functions, but no outage probability or health outcome is modeled.
notes: Infrastructure dependency is not disease burden.

subject: IDB-036
statement: County, sewershed, facility, watershed, program, and generalized regional scales remain distinct and are not downscaled to neighborhoods or individuals.
